items.summary: A Mississauga resident is one of two people charged in connection with a police investigation into drug trafficking in a Northern Ontario town. items.title: Ontario cop charged following stolen Hummer crash in Mississauga
items.summary: Ontario’s police watchdog agency has charged a Halton police officer following a crash while chasing a stolen Hummer over a year ago in Mississauga. m. at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Lakeshore Road East, on the border of Mississauga and Oakville. Officers with the Halton Regional Police Service had been investigating the theft of a Kia Sedona from a home in Oakville that also involved a stolen GMC Hummer, the SIU says. Investigators say the drivers of both vehicles fled the scene and officers attempted to stop them. Police gave chase led by Sgt. David Joseph, and the pursuit took officers through Oakville and Mississauga. That’s when the driver of the Hummer was involved in a collision with a diesel fuel truck tractor-trailer at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Lakeshore Road East. The 26-year-old driver of the Hummer was arrested and rushed to hospital with a serious injury, the SIU says. More than a year later, the SIU now says that Joseph has been charged with dangerous operation of a conveyance causing bodily harm. The accused is scheduled to make a court appearance in Milton on Nov. 23.

items.title: Italian sandwich shop brings its viral creations to Mississauga
items.summary: A Toronto sandwich shop that has attracted attention for its oversized Italian creations and freshly baked bread has opened a new location in Mississauga, bringing its popular menu to one of the city’s busiest shopping centres. Vero Italian Sandwich Co. has officially opened at Square One Shopping Centre, offering sandwiches built with imported Italian ingredients, specialty cheeses, cured meats and bread made through a lengthy fermentation process. The shop is located inside the mall’s food court. The business was founded around the vision of Chef Daniele Gagliotta, a world-champion pizza maker from Naples, Italy, who brought his expertise in dough-making to the sandwich business. Rather than using standard sandwich bread, Vero builds its creations on schiacciata, a traditional Italian flatbread similar to focaccia. The dough undergoes a 72-hour cold-fermentation process, which the company says helps produce a crisp exterior and light, airy interior. The bread is made using flour imported from Italy, while the sandwiches feature a variety of Italian deli meats, cheeses, spreads and fresh toppings. The preparation process is also part of the experience, with meats and cheeses sliced to order. Vero’s arrival in Mississauga marks another step in the brand’s expansion beyond its original Toronto location on Queen Street West. The company has also opened a location at Upper Canada Mall in Newmarket, making the Square One shop its third location. The menu features several signature sandwiches, including the Don Angelo, which combines prosciutto, burrata, Parmigiano cheese, tomato, balsamic glaze and arugula.

items.title: Halton police sergeant charged after chase of stolen Hummer ends in crash: SIU
items.summary: A Halton police officer has been charged after a stolen Hummer crashed into a tractor-trailer in Mississauga last year following a police chase, according to Ontario's Special Investigations Unit.

items.title: Mississauga election: Alvin Tedjo’s promises on affordability and safety
items.summary: From a property tax freeze to hiring more police officers, here are some of the promises Mississauga residents can expect from newly elected Mayor Alvin Tedjo. Tedjo won the Mississauga mayoral race on Oct. 26, defeating incumbent Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie. 9 per cent of ballots cast. His victory comes after a campaign centred on affordability, housing, public safety and traffic congestion. One of Tedjo’s biggest campaign promises was to freeze property taxes for all residents for two years. He says the plan would be achieved by cutting waste, implementing a hiring freeze and avoiding new spending that would increase costs for taxpayers. For seniors aged 65 and older, Tedjo has promised to make the property tax freeze permanent. Specific eligibility requirements would be developed in partnership with city council, according to his campaign platform. Tedjo has also pledged to increase the annual property tax rebate for low-income seniors from $571 to approximately $700, an adjustment he says would account for inflation. Tedjo has said crime and public safety have become increasingly serious concerns for Mississauga residents.

items.title: After Years of Resident Pressure, Mississauga Will Again Clear Snow Piles From Every Driveway
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga's winter maintenance crews will once again clear windrows, the heavy piles of snow and ice left at the end of driveways after plows pass, from every residential driveway in the city this winter. The outlet reports the city first offered this driveway-clearing service last winter after residents pushed city council for years to address the problem. Helen Noehammer, the city's director of works operations and maintenance, told insauga.com the service was well received overall last winter. According to the outlet, Noehammer is reminding residents to help the program run smoothly by moving parked vehicles off the street whenever the city declares a winter parking restriction during heavy snowfall. The outlet reports vehicles left on the road, including in areas with new 15-hour parking rules this year, could be fined $150 or towed. Insauga.com notes the reminder comes as cold, snowy weather approaches in the coming weeks.

items.title: Mississauga's Cycling Advisory Committee Opens Nominations for Its Annual Advocacy Awards
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, the city's Cycling Advisory Committee is accepting nominations through Jan. 8 for its 2026 cycling advocacy awards. The outlet reports the awards recognize residents, local businesses and students who promoted cycling and active transportation across Mississauga throughout the year. Nominees must live in Mississauga and must not have won a committee award within the past four years, according to mississauga.com. The outlet reports current committee members, city and Peel Region employees who work in cycling or sustainable transportation, and their immediate family, are not eligible. According to mississauga.com, anyone nominating someone must submit a form along with two supporting letters, and self-nominations are also accepted. The outlet reports the committee will review nominations and announce recipients at a council meeting in spring 2027.

items.title: Peel Public Health Hands Out Six Conditional Passes After Mississauga Restaurant Inspections
items.summary: According to Peel Public Health, six Mississauga restaurants received a conditional pass rather than the usual green sign during recent food safety inspections. The health unit said inspectors regularly check restaurants, cocktail bars, beverage rooms, bakeries and takeout establishments across the region to confirm compliance with the Health Protection and Promotion Act. Peel Public Health explained a green pass tells customers a business is meeting food safety and operational requirements, while a conditional pass signals an issue inspectors found. The health unit reports Aghati Restaurant, at 2575 Dundas St. in Mississauga, was inspected Oct. 27 and received a conditional pass. According to Peel Public Health, a second Mississauga location was inspected Oct. 22 as part of the same round of checks. The health unit's inspection program continues on a rolling basis throughout the year.

items.title: New Mayor's Affordability Push Freezes Mississauga's Big Arts-Centre Overhaul
items.summary: According to insauga.com, plans to tear down Mississauga's Living Arts Centre and replace it with a larger performing arts venue have stalled following Monday's mayoral election. The outlet reports mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo spoke to media at Celebration Square, steps from the LAC, the morning after his win and reiterated the affordability message from his campaign. Insauga.com says Tedjo argued that building an entirely new, costly downtown core featuring a convention centre, hotel and performing arts facility should not be a top priority during difficult financial times. The outlet reports the proposal originated earlier this year under outgoing mayor Carolyn Parrish and city council. According to insauga.com, Tedjo defeated Parrish by 22,626 votes and former mayor Bonnie Crombie by 31,288 votes, while Ward 7 Coun. Dipika Damerla finished fourth with 11,500 votes. The outlet notes it remains unclear whether the downtown plan will move forward now that a new mayor has taken office.

items.title: Culham Trail Access Point Reopens as Eglinton Avenue Sewer Upgrade Wraps Up
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Peel Region has finished upgrading the sanitary sewer and maintenance holes along a stretch of Eglinton Avenue West near Mississauga Road. According to the outlet, region officials said all construction work between Hewicks Lane and The Chase is now complete. The outlet reports the project upgraded sewers that carry wastewater from sinks, tubs, showers and toilets, a task officials said was needed to keep providing high-quality wastewater service. According to insauga.com, traffic on Eglinton Avenue West is expected to return to normal now that the work is done. The outlet reports the completed project also means the Eglinton Avenue West and Barbertown Road access point to the Culham Trail, closed to the public since earlier this year, will reopen.

items.title: Tedjo beat 2 incumbents in Mississauga's mayoral race. Here are his plans for the city
items.summary: One day after a decisive victory, Alvin Tedjo announced his priorities as the next mayor of Mississauga, saying he will focus on affordability, crime, housing, transportation and the economy.
